column1: # Planted scan roots for check_no_inline_tests.sh: the inline-block rule, its exemptions and its refusals.
# Columns, tab-separated, none empty ("-" for none): fixture (a directory beside this
# table), args (gate arguments, "{}" is the fixture path), stream (both, out or err: the
# gate's output the needles are read from), exit (exact), has (strings that must all
# appear), lacks (strings none of which may appear), is (the whole output; "\t" is a
# tab), what (what the case proves). Needles are fixed strings separated by ";;".
# Each root holds a crates/ tree. The rule bans an inline test module in a source file and
# allows the sibling-pointer form; a test file, an integration test and a build directory
# are not scanned. A root with nothing to scan is a refusal (exit 2), because an empty
# scan passes every rule it has.
